subject: QueryFoundry SDK + Redwood tracing adapter: integration plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@queryfoundry.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood + QueryFoundry SDK integration idea

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the intro last week — Daniel and I enjoyed the demo of Redwood's dedicated runtime. QueryFoundry builds an SDK used by ISVs to glue model chains, tooling, and telemetry together. We're seeing an increasing number of customers ask for an official Redwood adapter so they can route execution + traces through their orchestration layer.

High-level ask: partner on a small reference adapter that preserves Redwood's tracing + prompt metadata (request IDs, model variant, token usage, partial outputs for streaming) and exposes a lightweight shim that our SDK users can drop in. Ideally the adapter would also support function/tool invocation mapping so our tool-tracing correlates with Redwood call traces.

I've attached a short outline of what we had in mind (qf-integration-outline.pdf). Are you the right person to scope this, or should I loop in someone else from platform/partnerships?

Open to a quick 30-minute sync this week to sketch an action plan.

Best,
Elena
Director, Integrations
QueryFoundry
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@queryfoundry.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood + QueryFoundry SDK integration idea

Elena — thanks for the message and the outline. I'm the right contact for a proof-of-concept adapter; looping in Jasmine (platform SDK lead) and Olga (runtime/observability) to make sure we cover tracing semantics end-to-end.

Quick thoughts before a call:
- We can expose a tracing shim that translates QueryFoundry span tags into Redwood's trace fields (request_id, model_name, model_variant, latency_buckets).
- For streaming responses we'll emit incremental events with partial_token_count and cumulative_usage so the SDK can surface progress in their UI.
- Function/tool invocation: propose mapping QueryFoundry's tool call IDs to Redwood's tool_call_id and including the full tool response as an attached payload in the trace for easier replay.

I've sketched a short proposal (redwood-trace-shim-proposal.md) — attaching it here. Can we meet Thu 2/26 10:00 PT? I've added a tentative calendar link.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Developer Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Sounds great. One thing to call out from our side: several of our ISV customers use prompt templating and evaluation tools that record prompt versions and test prompts. We'll want the adapter to capture prompt template IDs + eval run ids (example: promptset_id) so downstream audits can correlate a generated response back to the originating prompt version.

Noted on the call. See you Thu.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Folks — great call today. Summarizing our mutual action plan and owners below. I'm attaching an initial integration map (integration-map-v1.xlsx) and a sequence diagram for trace correlation (sequence-diagram.png).

Mutual action plan (MVP):
1) Trace shim spec (owner: Redwood - Olga) — map QueryFoundry span tags to Redwood trace model; include fields: request_id, parent_span, model_variant, token_usage (per-chunk + cumulative), tool_call_id, promptset_id. Deliverable: open spec and sample JSON trace.
2) Reference adapter (owner: QueryFoundry - Daniel) — lightweight npm package that implements the shim and a small example showing streaming + function calls. Deliverable: repo with tests and readme.
3) Example integration app (owner: Redwood - Jasmine) — simple Next.js demo that shows end-to-end traces surfaced in Redwood Console and QueryFoundry UI. Deliverable: demo repo + test prompts.
4) QA & rollout plan (owner: joint) — run with 2 beta customers, validate metrics, gap analysis, then public docs. Deliverable: beta feedback doc + release checklist.

Timeline: 4–6 weeks for MVP with weekly syncs. Next steps: Daniel to create the adapter repo skeleton, Olga will publish the trace shim draft by Mon 3/2, Jasmine will start the demo scaffold.

Related links:
- Proposal repo (w/ initial issue): https://github.com/queryfoundry/redwood-adapter/tree/proposal
- Meeting notes + calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=call-20260225-qf-rw

If there are any missing pieces or clarifications, flag them here.

Thanks all,
Marcus

> Folks — great call today. Summarizing our mutual action plan and owners below. I'm attaching an initial integration map (integration-map-v1.xlsx) and a sequence diagram for trace correlation (sequence-diagram.png).

This looks good — Daniel will open the repo today and add the adapter skeleton. We'll aim to have a first working prototype that streams tokens and emits trace events by the end of week 2.

One quick ask from our security team: will the adapter include any credentials or secret handling patterns we should align on? We prefer not to embed long-lived tokens in the adapter; would Redwood support a short-lived credential flow or an ephemeral token exchange for demo/beta customers?

If Redwood can share recommended secrets patterns (brief doc), we'll include that in the repo. Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,
Elena
